sentences.text: Santorini -LRB- Σαντορίνη , pronounced -LSB- sandoˈrini -RSB- -RRB- , classically Thera -LRB- English pronunciation -LSB- ˈθɪərə -RSB- -RRB- , and officially Thira -LRB- Greek : Θήρα -LSB- ˈθira -RSB- -RRB- , is an island in the southern Aegean Sea , about 200 km southeast of Greece 's mainland .	Thira	Thira (regional unit)	English	English language	Greek	Greek language	Aegean Sea	Aegean Sea	Greece	Greece
It is the largest island of a small , circular archipelago which bears the same name and is the remnant of a volcanic caldera .	archipelago	archipelago	volcanic	volcano	caldera	caldera
It forms the southernmost member of the Cyclades group of islands , with an area of approximately 73 km2 and a 2011 census population of 15,550 .	Cyclades	Cyclades

The municipality of Santorini includes the inhabited islands of Santorini and Therasia and the uninhabited islands of Nea Kameni , Palaia Kameni , Aspronisi , and Christiana .	Therasia	Therasia	Nea Kameni	Nea Kameni	Palaia Kameni	Palaia Kameni	Aspronisi	Aspronisi
The total land area is 90.623 km2 .
Santorini is part of the Thira regional unit .	Thira	Thira (regional unit)	Thira regional unit	Thira (regional unit)

Santorini is essentially what remains after an enormous volcanic eruption that destroyed the earliest settlements on a formerly single island , and created the current geological caldera .	volcanic	volcano	caldera	caldera	volcanic eruption	volcanic eruption
A giant central , rectangular lagoon , which measures about 12 by , is surrounded by 300 m high , steep cliffs on three sides .
The main island slopes downward to the Aegean Sea .	Aegean Sea	Aegean Sea

On the fourth side , the lagoon is separated from the sea by another much smaller island called Therasia ; the lagoon is connected to the sea in two places , in the northwest and southwest .	Therasia	Therasia

The depth of the caldera , at 400m , makes it impossible for any but the largest ships to anchor anywhere in the protected bay ; there is also a fisherman 's harbour at Vlychada , on the southwestern coast .	caldera	caldera
The island 's principal port is Athinios .
The capital , Fira , clings to the top of the cliff looking down on the lagoon .	Fira	Fira
The volcanic rocks present from the prior eruptions feature olivine , and have a small presence of hornblende .	volcanic	volcano	olivine	olivine	hornblende	hornblende

It is the most active volcanic centre in the South Aegean Volcanic Arc , though what remains today is chiefly a water-filled caldera .	South Aegean	South Aegean	volcanic	volcano	caldera	caldera	South Aegean Volcanic Arc	South Aegean Volcanic Arc
The volcanic arc is approximately 500 km long and 20 to wide .	volcanic	volcano

The region first became volcanically active around 3 -- 4 million years ago , though volcanism on Thera began around 2 million years ago with the extrusion of dacitic lavas from vents around the Akrotiri .	Akrotiri	Akrotiri (Santorini)

The island is the site of one of the largest volcanic eruptions in recorded history : the Minoan eruption -LRB- sometimes called the Thera eruption -RRB- , which occurred some 3,600 years ago at the height of the Minoan civilization .	volcanic	volcano	Minoan eruption	Minoan eruption	Minoan civilization	Minoan civilization

The eruption left a large caldera surrounded by volcanic ash deposits hundreds of metres deep and may have led indirectly to the collapse of the Minoan civilization on the island of Crete , 110 km to the south , through a gigantic tsunami .	volcanic	volcano	caldera	caldera	Minoan civilization	Minoan civilization	volcanic ash	volcanic ash	Crete	Crete	tsunami	tsunami
Another popular theory holds that the Thera eruption is the source of the legend of Atlantis .	Atlantis	Atlantis
